(1) LBAs are a viable approach for reducing the overhead of runtime monitoring, and (2) a key challenge for LBAs is how to efficiently deliver the main program's trace to a monitoring program.
log-based architectures (LBAs) can dramatically reduce the overheads of monitoring deployed code and that LBAs have the potential to significantly improve the reliability of deployed code.
log-based architectures are an effective way to reduce overhead of program monitoring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the design and implementation of LBA, a new architecture paradigm that enables the efficient and effective use of on-chip resources to perform general purpose runtime monitoring of deployed code.
the design of a hardware/software infrastructure to support general-purpose runtime monitoring in deployed code.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LBA can reduce monitoring overheads by an order of 10-100x.
the proposed architecture can be used to significantly reduce the overhead of monitoring tasks.
the proposed LBA is a promising approach for general-purpose monitoring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the log-based architecture (LBA) is an attractive approach to the problem of monitoring deployed code.
we advocate a new architecture for runtime monitoring of deployed software.
we advocate the use of LBA for general purpose monitoring of deployed code and we provide the first detailed study of the design space for such architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LBAs offer a general-purpose approach to runtime program monitoring that can be used for a wide range of monitoring tasks.
LBAs are a promising architecture for general purpose program monitoring.
LBAs provide an effective means of reducing the overhead of runtime monitoring, while still allowing for the monitoring of deployed code.
